method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Aims: prevent hypoglycaemia during and after surgery, and acute hyperglycaemia ± ketosis after it.**
claims.source_text: The major aims are to prevent hypoglycaemia during and after surgery and acute hyperglycaemia +/- ketosis after surgery.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Plan elective surgery in advance with the endocrinology team**, who oversee peri-operative diabetes management during the admission.
claims.source_text: Elective surgery should be planned in advance in consultation with the endocrinology team … During the admission, the endocrinology team will oversee the peri-operative management of diabetes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Major** = GA over 2 hours or prolonged post-operative fasting expected. **Minor** = GA under 2 hours, with oral intake expected to resume before same-day discharge.
claims.source_text: 'Major': GA of >2 hours or prolonged period of fasting anticipated in the post-operative period … 'Minor': GA of <2 hours duration; anticipated to resume oral intake prior to discharge on the same day
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Minor surgery: aim for a morning list with the child first on it**, and preferably admit the day before.
claims.source_text: Aim for morning surgery and for the child with diabetes to be first on the surgical list. … It is preferable to have child admitted the day before surgery.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Evening before: give the full usual short-acting dose and 75% of the usual long-acting dose** before the evening meal.
claims.source_text: Prior to their evening meal on the night before the procedure the child should receive: Their full usual dose of short-acting insulin, along with 75% of their usual long acting insulin dose
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Morning list:** check BGL 2 1/2 hours before surgery (~6.00 a.m.). **Under 8.0 mmol/L: a sugar-containing clear drink (10% sugar, e.g. lemonade) 5–10 mL/kg, max 200 mL**, and note it for the anaesthetist.
claims.source_text: 2 1/2 hours before surgery (~6.00 a.m.) a BGL should be performed … If BGL is below 8.0 mmol/L, the child should be given a drink of lemonade or other palatable sugar-containing clear fluid (10% sugar). The amount given should be between 5 and 10 mL/kg body weight with a maximum of 200 mL
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Morning of surgery (~7.30–8.00am): 1/10th of the normal total daily insulin as short-acting insulin, rounded down to the nearest whole unit.**
claims.source_text: 1/10th of the normal total daily insulin requirement should be given as short acting insulin on the morning before surgery (~7.30-8.00am). This calculation should be rounded down to the nearest whole unit.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any BGL under 4.0 mmol/L in the 2 hours before surgery: site an IV, give 2–5 mL/kg of 10% dextrose as a bolus, then start dextrose-containing fluids at maintenance** (e.g. Plasma-Lyte 148 + 5% glucose with 20 mmol/L KCl, or 0.9% sodium chloride + 5% glucose with 20 mmol/L KCl).
claims.source_text: if any BGL is <4.0 mmol/L within the 2 hours prior to surgery, an i.v line will need to be sited and 2-5 mL/kg of 10% dextrose given as an i.v bolus, before commencing dextrose-containing i.v. fluids (eg Plasma-Lyte 148 and 5% Glucose with 20 mmol/L KCl OR 0.9% sodium chloride (normal saline) and 5% Glucose with 20 mmol/L KCl) at the child's maintenance requirements
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check BGL hourly during and after surgery until tolerating oral intake**, including immediately before transfer to and from theatre. **Aim for 5–10 mmol/L.**
claims.source_text: BGL should be checked hourly intra- and post- operatively (including a level immediately prior to transfer to and from theatre) until tolerating oral intake … Aim to keep BGL in the range 5 - 10 mmol/L
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A further short-acting dose (~15–20% of total daily dose) is needed before lunch.** If unexpectedly not tolerating oral diet, give it 4–6 hours after the morning dose and continue IV fluids.
claims.source_text: The child will need a further dose of short acting insulin (~15-20% of total daily dose) before lunch. If unexpectedly not tolerating oral diet, give this additional insulin dose 4-6 hours after the morning dose and continue i.v. fluids.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Usually discharged the same afternoon**, with advice to take the usual insulin dose before the evening meal.
claims.source_text: In general patients will be discharged home in the afternoon after minor surgery. Advice should be given to have their usual dose of insulin prior to evening meal
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Afternoon list:** 1/10th of total daily insulin as short-acting at ~07.00am before a light breakfast of 2–3 carbohydrate serves, **then another 1/10th at ~12.00 noon without food.**
claims.source_text: On the morning of surgery at ~07.00am, 1/10th of normal total daily insulin dose should be given as short acting insulin before a light breakfast consisting of 2-3 carbohydrate serves … An additional injection of short acting insulin at 1/10th of total daily dose is given at ~12.00 noon, without food as the patient will be fasting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Evening basal insulin: give the usual dose the night before**, cut by ~20% if there is a recent pattern of overnight or early-morning hypos. **Morning basal users: full dose the day before, 80% on the morning of surgery.**
claims.source_text: The usual dose of basal insulin can be given the night before, unless there is a recent pattern of overnight or early morning hypos, in which case the dose should be decreased by ~20% … If the patient takes basal insulin in the morning, then they should have their full dose of basal insulin on the day before surgery and 80% of their usual basal insulin dose on the morning of surgery
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Morning list: no short- or rapid-acting insulin before surgery** — the basal dose suffices. Oral fluid only if the 06.00am BGL is under 6.0 mmol/L: **lemonade 5–10 mL/kg, max 200 mL.**
claims.source_text: Short / rapid acting insulin is not needed before surgery as the background lantus dose will suffice. Patients on this regimen therefore only need oral fluids if the BGL at 06.00am is <6.0 mmol/L, when lemonade (5-10 mL/kg; max 200 mL) can be given.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Afternoon list: 80% of the usual rapid-acting dose with a usual-carbohydrate breakfast**; check BGL 2.5 hours before surgery and give clear sugar-containing fluid 5–10 mL/kg (max 200 mL) if under 6.0 mmol/L.
claims.source_text: Give 80% of usual rapid-acting insulin with breakfast containing the patient's usual number of carbohydrate serves … Check BGL 2.5 hours prior to surgery and give clear sugar-containing fluids (5-10 mL/kg, up to 200 mL max) if BGL is <6.0 mmol/L
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Once tolerating oral diet**, give the usual rapid-acting dose before a usual-carbohydrate meal and stop IV fluids.
claims.source_text: Once tolerating oral diet, the patient can have their usual rapid-acting insulin dose before a meal consisting of their usual carbohydrate serves. I.V. fluids can then cease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Insulin pumps cannot be worn for procedures involving screening or radiation** (e.g. cardiac catheterisation) — plan insulin delivery with endocrinology in advance.
claims.source_text: Please note that insulin pumps can NOT be worn for procedures that involve screening / exposure to radiation (eg cardiac catheterisation). … Please discuss such cases and a plan for insulin delivery with the endocrinology team in advance of any such procedures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Change the subcutaneous infusion site the day before surgery**, early enough for at least 2 BGL checks showing the line works.
claims.source_text: The patient should be advised to change the subcutaneous infusion site on the day before surgery. This should be done in time to have at least 2 subsequent BGL checks on that day that indicate the line is working well
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **06.00am BGL on a morning list:** under 4.0 mmol/L — sugar-containing clear fluid 5–10 mL/kg (max 200 mL) **and a temporary basal rate of 70% for 4 hours**; 4.0–10.0 — **70% temporary basal for 4 hours**; over 10.0 — enter the BGL, give the pump's correction dose, **and 70% temporary basal for 4 hours.**
claims.source_text: If BGL is <4.0 mmol/L, give 5-10 mL/kg (up to a max of 200 mL) of sugar-containing clear fluids (eg lemonade) and commence a temporary basal rate of 70% of usual for 4 hours … If BGL is between 4.0 and 10.0 mmol/L, commence a temporary basal rate of 70% of their usual rate for 4 hours … If BGL at 06.00am is >10.0 mmol/L, program the BGL into the pump and give the recommended correction dose of insulin. A temporary reduction in basal to 70% of usual should also be commenced for 4 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The pump can continue through surgery at the programmed basal rate**; secure the infusion site tightly before theatre.
claims.source_text: The subcutaneous infusion site should be secured tightly prior to going to theatre to prevent dislodgement and interruption to insulin delivery intra-operatively … CSII can be continued during the surgery / procedure using the basal rate as programmed above
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intra-operative BGL under 4.0 mmol/L: 2–5 mL/kg 10% dextrose IV bolus**, then start dextrose-containing fluids or increase the dextrose concentration of those running.
claims.source_text: If BGL drops below 4.0mmol/l administer 2-5 mL/kg 10% dextrose as an i.v. bolus and commence dextrose containing iv fluids (or increase the dextrose concentration of fluids running)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Admit the day before, ideally for a morning list, and site an IV on the day of admission.**
claims.source_text: The child should be admitted the day before and ideally surgery should take place on a morning list … An i.v. line should be sited on the day of admission
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At ~06.00am start an IV insulin infusion plus maintenance fluids of 0.9% sodium chloride + 5% glucose with 20 mmol/L KCl.**
claims.source_text: At ~06.00am an intravenous insulin infusion and maintenance intravenous fluids (0.9% sodium chloride (normal saline) and 5% Glucose with 20 mmol/L KCl) should be commenced
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infusion: 50 units regular insulin (Actrapid or Humulin R) in 49.5 mL 0.9% NaCl = 1 unit/mL**, on a syringe pump, clearly labelled.
claims.source_text: The insulin infusion is made up by adding 50 units of regular insulin (Actrapid or Humulin R) to 49.5 ml 0.9% NaCl (1 unit/ml solution) … provided a syringe pump is used. Ensure that the insulin is clearly labelled
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start at 0.02–0.03 U/kg/hr — much lower than the DKA rate**; 0.03 U/kg/hr if BGL is over 10.0 mmol/L. **Pump users: stop the pump half an hour after IV insulin and fluids start.**
claims.source_text: The initial rate of the insulin infusion should be 0.02 - 0.03 U/kg/hr (note that this maintenance rate is much lower than the rate required to treat DKA) … 0.03 U/kg/hr if BGL >10.0 mmol/L … subcutaneous insulin via the pump should be discontinued half an hour after i.v. insulin and i.v. fluids are commenced
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Titrate to BGL 5.0–10.0 mmol/L, checked hourly:** 2 consecutive hourly BGLs over 10.0 — **increase by 0.005–0.01 U/kg/hr**; any BGL under 5.0 — decrease by the same step; **already at 0.02 U/kg/hr — raise IV dextrose to 10%** instead.
claims.source_text: BGLs should be monitored hourly while on an insulin infusion … Aim to keep BGLs between 5.0 and 10.0 mmol/L … If 2 consecutive hourly BGLs are above 10.0 mmol/L, the insulin infusion rate should be increased by 0.005-0.01 U/kg/hr … If any BGL is <5.0 mmol/L, the insulin rate can be decreased by the same increment (0.005-0.01U/kg/hr) to prevent hypoglycaemia. If the insulin rate is already at 0.02U/kg/hr, increase the dextrose concentration of i.v. fluids to 10%
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Any BGL over 15.0 mmol/L: check blood ketones at the bedside.**
claims.source_text: If any BGL is >15.0 mmol/L, check blood ketones with a bedside test
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transition back to subcutaneous insulin is individual**, agreed with the diabetes team; CSII can restart post-op even while nil by mouth, set by endocrinology.
claims.source_text: Transition back to subcutaneous insulin in the post-op period should be discussed on an individual basis with the diabetes team … It is possible to recommence CSII in the post-operative period even if the patient is being kept nil by mouth; this should be done by the endocrinology team who will recommend rates and settings on an individual basis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Contact the endocrinology team / consultant on call for every child with diabetes needing emergency surgery.** Assess first: blood gas with glucose, bedside ketones, U&E, FBE and other pre-op bloods.
claims.source_text: The Endocrinology team / consultant on call should be contacted about all patients with diabetes who require emergency surgery … the child should first be assessed clinically and biochemically (blood gas including glucose and bedside ketones test, along with U&E, FBE and other pre-op bloods as required)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ketoacidosis present: start the DKA protocol immediately and stabilise circulating volume and electrolytes before surgery.** Initial insulin is 0.1 U/kg/hr, continued until ketones clear and acidosis corrects.
claims.source_text: If ketoacidosis is present, treatment according to the diabetic ketoacidosis protocol should be commenced immediately and the patient's circulating volume and electrolytes stabilised before surgery … Where DKA is present, initial insulin infusion rates will be 0.1 U/kg/hr … This rate should be continued until ketones have cleared and acidosis has corrected
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After DKA clears**, maintenance insulin is usually 0.02–0.03 U/kg/hr, with dextrose adjusted to keep BGL 5–10 mmol/L; endocrinology advises.
claims.source_text: the insulin infusion rates may be reduced and the dextrose concentration of i.v. fluids adjusted as appropriate to maintain BGLs between 5-10 mmol/L. Maintenance insulin infusion rates once ketosis/acidosis has fully cleared are usually in the range of 0.02-0.03 U/kg/hr; the endocrinology team will advise on this
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No ketoacidosis: fast the child and start 0.9% sodium chloride + 5% glucose with 20 mmol/L KCl plus a continuous IV insulin infusion** — same make-up, starting rate and titration as major elective surgery.
claims.source_text: If there is no ketoacidosis, the child should be fasted and commenced on intravenous dextrose/saline (start with 0.9% sodium chloride (normal saline) and 5% Glucose with 20mmol/l KCl) along with continuous IV insulin infusion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus and surgery' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus_and_surgery/, retrieved 2026-09-23
